question.problem:
Consider the Poisson distribution $\text{Po}(5).$ Rounding to $4$ decimal digits, fill in the missing values in the corresponding table for the cumulative distribution function below.

| $\,x\,$ | $0$ | $1$ | $2$ | $3$ | $4$ | $5$ | $6$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $P(X\le x)$ | {{field-1}} | {{field-2}} | $\,0.1247\,$ | $\,0.2650\,$ | $\,0.4405\,$ | $\,0.6160\,$ | $\,0.7622\,$ |
question.worked_solution:
The cumulative distribution function of a discrete random variable $X$ is a function $F(x)$ such that

$$
F(x)=P(X\le x).
$$

The probability mass function for the Poisson distribution $\text{Po}(\lambda )$ is given by

$$
f(x)=\frac{{\lambda }^{x}{e}^{-\lambda }}{x!},\,x=0,1,2,3,…\,.
$$

In our case, $\lambda =5.$ 

Therefore, we compute the missing elements of the table as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}F(0) & =P(X\le 0) \\  & =P(X=0) \\  & =\frac{{5}^{0}{e}^{-5}}{0!} \\  & =\frac{1\cdot {e}^{-5}}{1} \\  & ≈0.0067.\end{aligned}
$$

$$
\begin{aligned}F(1) & =P(X\le 1) \\  & =P(X=0)+P(X=1) \\  & =\frac{{5}^{0}\cdot {e}^{-5}}{0!}+\frac{{5}^{1}\cdot {e}^{-5}}{1!} \\  & =\frac{1\cdot {e}^{-5}}{1}+\frac{5\cdot {e}^{-5}}{1} \\  & ≈0.0404.\end{aligned}
$$
